import logging

def test_clear_then_add(caplog) -> None:
    """Test that after clear, new records are captured."""
    logging.warning("before clear")
    assert len(caplog.records) == 1
    caplog.clear()
    assert len(caplog.records) == 0
    logging.warning("after clear")
    assert len(caplog.records) == 1
    assert caplog.records[0].getMessage() == "after clear"

def test_clear_multiple_times(caplog) -> None:
    """Test multiple clears work correctly."""
    logging.warning("test1")
    logging.warning("test2")
    assert len(caplog.records) == 2
    caplog.clear()
    assert len(caplog.records) == 0
    caplog.clear()  # Clear empty list
    assert len(caplog.records) == 0
    logging.warning("test3")
    assert len(caplog.records) == 1

def test_get_records_after_clear(caplog) -> None:
    """Test that get_records returns correct results after clear."""
    logging.warning("before clear")
    caplog.clear()
    logging.warning("after clear")
    records = caplog.get_records("call")
    assert len(records) == 1
    assert records[0].getMessage() == "after clear"

def test_consistency_maintained(caplog) -> None:
    """Test that records and get_records stay in sync."""
    def verify():
        assert caplog.get_records("call") == caplog.records

    verify()
    logging.warning("test")
    verify()
    caplog.clear()
    verify()
    logging.warning("test2")
    verify()
    caplog.clear()
    verify()
